summary:
A Victorian terrace of three. Two mirrored red-brick end houses with cream canted bays, stoops and small black-slate mansards with dormers stand either side of a taller cream-stucco centre house with a quartz portico, a balcony and a bracketed flat parapet. They share a plinth, a string course and a cornice line, and the roofline steps up in the middle, so the row reads as three separate houses that belong together. I checked the roof spec on a mock shell: the mansards built with no warnings. The centre house's flat roof gives one warning (the deck is a single material), which I left because the parapet hides the deck from the street. Victorian terrace: red-brick A and C with canted bays and slate mansards flank a taller cream-stucco B with quartz portico, balcony and bracketed parapet.
Two party-wall chimney stacks with lit campfires, four hearths, three stair wells, street, trees and walled rear gardens.
Six parts along the trades: shell, stairs, roofs, chimneys, fenestration and front, grounds.

concept_subject: A Victorian townhouse terrace of three attached houses on a city street, seen from the pavement. The two end houses are red brick, three storeys over a grey stone-brick plinth. Each has a two-storey canted bay window of cream sandstone with large glass panes on its inner side, and a three-step stone stoop with a black railing on its outer side leading to a painted front door: teal on the left house, crimson on the right. Each door has a glass transom and a white quartz hood on brackets. A cream sandstone string course runs along the row above the ground floor, the outer corners have paired cream quoins, every window has a cream sill and lintel, and there are flower boxes under the top-floor windows. Each end house is capped by a stone dentil cornice and a small black-slate mansard roof with one gabled dormer and an iron crest. Between them stands the centre house, one storey taller, in smooth cream stucco. Its front door is dark oak behind a white quartz portico of two columns, and the flat portico roof is a first-floor balcony with an iron railing, reached through a French door. It has a row of three tall windows on each floor, a quartz bracketed cornice and a flat parapet with an iron rail at the top. Its side walls show above the neighbours' mansards, and cream stone pilaster strips mark the party walls between the houses. Two tall brick chimney stacks with dark bands and smoking caps rise on the party walls through the roofs. In front: black iron area railings, a grey flagstone pavement with a kerb, two lamp posts and three young street trees, then an andesite road. Behind: three walled back gardens with paths and gates.
